subject: Dedicated reservation: GPU fitment & throughput checklist for CloudFlora RFP
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@cloudflora.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: cloudflora-arch <infra@cloudflora.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CloudFlora RFP — Dedicated GPU sizing worksheet attached

Hi Tessa / Marcus,

Thanks for the demo last week — as discussed, I'm attaching our completed RFP worksheet and a sampled workload dump (small subset). Our procurement & infra teams need a recommended reservation plan keyed to throughput (tokens/sec), tail-latency targets, and GPU family fit. High-level constraints:
- Region: US-west primary, with DR in US-east
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 300ms for user-facing chat flows (~1–2k tokens responses)
- Cost target: target blended cost <$0.60 per 1k tokens (we know this depends on batch/quant)
- Usage mix: 70% short-chat (<2k tokens), 20% long-context (8–32k), 10% high-volume embeddings
- Desired commitment window: 12–36 months with burst capacity for seasonal traffic

Questions we need answered in the RFP response:
1) Recommended GPU families & counts by region for a 12-month commit to meet throughput and latency SLOs (give both baseline reserved and burst pool sizes).
2) How you model KV cache hit rates and what reserve reduction we can expect if we enable prefix caching for the chat flows.
3) Fallback strategy if the primary GPU pool is saturated (latency-aware routing to lower-cost variants).
4) Attach any pricing/workbook assumptions and a sample token-cost calculation for our traffic profile.

I've attached: CF-RFP-Dedicated-Worksheet.xlsx and cloudflora-workload-sample.csv. Can you turn around a response by EOD Wednesday?

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Head of Infrastructure Procurement
CloudFlora Inc.

Hi Priya — thanks for the worksheet and the sample traces, this is very helpful. Below is a concise recommendation we can drop into the RFP response; I'll attach the detailed workbook and a token-cost worked example (see attachments). If this looks good we can expand numbers into a formal commitment proposal.

Executive recommendation (US-west primary, 12-month commit, with regional DR):
- Baseline reserved pool (steady-state): 8x H100-80GB (latency-critical chat), 6x A100-80GB (long-context 32k), 4x L4-sized T4-class nodes (cheap embeddings and background batch jobs).
- Burst pool: additional 6x H100-equivalent slots (elastic burst tied to monthly caps).
- Autoscale policy: horizontal scale on queued requests with max concurrency per slot tuned to keep 95p latency <= 300ms for short-chat (empirically we use concurrency=3 for H100 for 1–2k token responses).

Throughput modeling & assumptions (summary):
- Short-chat (1–2k) on H100: ~850–1,100 tokens/sec per GPU when batching is enabled and KV cache hit rate is 30–40%. We recommend enabling prefix cache for chat sessions — expect ~25–35% reduction in token compute for repeat contexts.
- Long-context (8–32k) on A100: throughput depends heavily on sequence length; estimate ~250–400 tokens/sec per GPU for 32k sequences with mixed attention optimizations.
- Embeddings on L4-class: ~12–18k embeddings/sec per node (small memory, cost-efficient).

Fallbacks and graceful degradation:
1) Region fallback: route to US-east reserved pool (DR) if US-west is saturated.
2) Model variant fallback: routing policy to degrade from H100 standard to A100 quantized variant for lower cost with slight latency increase.
3) Priority lanes: user-facing traffic gets served from dedicated low-latency lanes; batch/async jobs are queued into low-priority pool.

Attachments in this email: redwood-dedicated-fitment-proposal.pdf (detailed workbook), dedicated-token-cost-example.xlsx (token-cost breakout).

A few quick follow-ups where we need input from CloudFlora before finalizing counts:
- Expected % of requests that will hit prefix cache (do you have session stickiness and reuse patterns?)
- Any hard cost cap per 1M tokens you want guaranteed in the proposal (will affect our suggested quantization & batch targets).

If you want, Marcus can run a short sizing-run with your sample CSV to produce a pro forma 12-month spend with monthly burn & burst allowances.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-dedicated-fitment-proposal.pdf, dedicated-token-cost-example.xlsx

Hi Priya — looping in our pricing and reliability notes as requested. Below is the delta table and the SLA/canary sketch we propose. We're happy to add a contract amendment template for mid-term burst.

Delta table (baseline vs shift 2 H100 -> 3 A100):
- Baseline (8 H100 + 6 A100): 95p latency for short-chat: ~260ms; estimated effective tokens/sec for short-chat (aggregate): ~7k–8.5k tokens/sec across pool.
- Variant (6 H100 + 9 A100): 95p latency for short-chat: ~320–360ms (depends on batching); aggregate tokens/sec similar but higher variance on tail. 
- Cost delta (approx): Variant is ~12% lower monthly reserved cost but increases tail-latency risk; recommended only if your product tolerates 95p up to 350ms.

KV cache sensitivity guidance:
- If prefix cache hit rate moves from 30% -> 50%: recommended baseline H100 pool can be reduced by ~1–2 slots (we model 1 slot ~= 10–12% of short-chat pool capacity).
- Conservative commit: assume 30% hit rate for initial sizing; plan a 30–60 day measurement window and then execute an amendment to right-size reserved pool once steady-state reuse is observed.

SLA / failover & canary sequence (sketch):
1) Pre-warm DR pool continuously at low level (10% baseline) to keep model warm.
2) Automated health checks: if queue depth > X for >30s in US-west, start routing 20% of new traffic to DR for 5 mins while verifying 95p latency.
3) If DR maintains 95p <= 350ms for 5 consecutive minutes, increase routing incrementally in 20% steps until latency restored.
4) Post-incident: automatic rollback of routing to US-west with 1-hour cooldown to avoid thrash.

Billing & commercial: quarterly billing checkpoints for year-1 are supported; we will add a billing schedule to the SOW. Mid-term burst: we can provide a standard DocuSign amendment template to add burst capacity and prorate remaining term.

Next steps:
- Tessa / Marcus will attach a short pro forma (spreadsheet) showing monthly burn & burst headroom for both baseline and variant; we'll also attach the DocuSign amendment template.
- If you agree with the canary sketch, we'll include it in the SOW as an operational play and produce a short runbook.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Director, Product Operations — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-delta-costs-and-sla.xlsx, RS-DocuSign-Amendment-sample.pdf
